name: Rites of Spring
label: Dischord
lede: Fifteen shows, one LP, a four-song single, and a genre name they spent the next forty years refusing to answer to.

eras.title: Springtime for a stale scene
eras.text: By 1983 D.C. hardcore had grown bigger, meaner and more predictable, and a lot of the kids who built it had lost the thread. Three veterans of a hardcore band called Insurrection and a guitarist from The Faith set out to keep the speed and throw out the macho pose.

years.h: Out of Insurrection
years.p: [[Guy Picciotto|f8200cea-b5e9-4145-b5a5-1d0838f2c288]], [[Brendan Canty|8b505ef0-c5a7-4deb-bc32-27c882f3c40e]] and [[Mike Fellows|58a7226f-e06a-4728-82a5-ddc4443025a4]] had played hardcore together in Insurrection. By December they're writing the first songs: All There Is, End on End, By Design.

years.h: Named for a riot
years.p: The name comes from Stravinsky's The Rite of Spring, the ballet whose 1913 premiere ended in uproar. Picciotto liked the double meaning too: a springtime for a D.C. scene that had gone stale.

years.h: The first shows, and the gear doesn't always survive
years.p: Dischord dates the band's live life from spring 1984. They'd play only fifteen shows in all, and they played every one like it might be the last, sometimes wrecking their own equipment on the way out.

years.h: Six songs at Inner Ear, MacKaye at the board
years.p: With [[Eddie Janney|323dd1dd-23e4-45ce-9aa9-c5492096d604]], ex-[[The Faith|f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574]], now on second guitar, they cut a six-song demo at Inner Ear in Arlington with [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] producing. It sits unreleased for 28 years.

years.h: The bass player moves to California. They keep practicing anyway.
years.p: Fellows heads west and the others rehearse without him, assuming he's gone for good. About three months later he's back.

eras.title: Revolution Summer
eras.text: For one season, D.C. punk turned outward and inward at once: benefit shows, protests at the South African Embassy, and bands singing about things hardcore usually shrugged off. Rites of Spring were at the center of it, with the record to prove it.

years.h: Twelve songs, two producers
years.p: Back at Inner Ear, with MacKaye and [[Michael Hampton|4ed83c42-6348-4368-903e-9116bfa49b8e]] of The Faith producing, the band records the twelve songs that become its only album.

years.h: Rites of Spring · Dischord No. 16
years.p: Hardcore speed with the anger turned inward: confessional, melodic, and about the things punk usually kept quiet. Later reissues add the single and retitle it End on End.
years.xp:
The band pointed to The Smiths, Wire, the Buzzcocks and The Birthday Party, and to The Faith's 1983 EP Subject to Change, which had already shown that a D.C. hardcore band could turn the lens on itself.

Critics have described the record as swinging between fast and furious and lush, but never losing its drive or its melody.

q: Punk is about building things, not destroying them.
years.h: A show becomes a call to action
years.p: At the Chevy Chase Community Center, Rites of Spring use the stage to announce the first Punk Percussion Protest: punks with drums outside the South African Embassy, making noise against apartheid.
years.xp:
The embassy protests had been running since November 1984. The punk version came a week later, on June 21, pitched as noise loud enough to be heard inside the building. That night Rites of Spring played the 9:30 Club and Picciotto thanked the crowd for showing up.

The gear-smashing reputation followed them anyway. At a 9:30 Club show, Picciotto drew the line himself.

years.h: Two summer-job kids name a movement
years.p: Amy Pickering, who worked at Dischord, and Chris Thomson coined "Revolution Summer" at a city summer-jobs office, as an inside joke about revolting against their supervisor. It ended up naming a whole season of D.C. bands.

years.h: A joke from across the bill
years.p: On a night with [[Dag Nasty|4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192]], Rites of Spring and [[Embrace|9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431]], Dag Nasty guitarist [[Brian Baker|1fd36abf-e43c-4b01-820b-d7280cc27ea5]] says he came up with "emocore" to make fun of the Rites of Spring set. That's his own account, told to Parade in 2025.
years.xp:
Baker said he didn't think of it as coining anything at the time. Only years later did a friend point out where the word had come from.

Whoever said it first, the band never used it about itself.

eras.title: Four more songs, then gone
eras.text: Rites of Spring ended the way they played: fast, with no speech. They cut one last session in January and split within weeks, and three of them were in a new band before summer.

years.h: The All Through a Life session
years.p: Four songs at Inner Ear, produced by MacKaye and the band. It's the last thing the four of them record as Rites of Spring.

years.h: Done, less than two years after the first show
years.p: The band splits shortly after the session. Dischord closes the book in winter 1986: fifteen shows, one LP, one single still in the can.

years.h: [[One Last Wish|94f18045-7fe2-41df-bf24-0bed21c88eb8]]: three of them, plus Hampton
years.p: Picciotto, Janney and Canty start a new band with Embrace guitarist Michael Hampton. They play out from August and record an album at Inner Ear in November.

eras.title: Same people, different names
eras.text: The band was over, but the people weren't done with each other. In eighteen months they went through two more bands, and then two of them walked into Fugazi.

years.h: One Last Wish ends, and the album gets shelved
years.p: The band breaks up after mixing the record. Dischord holds off on releasing it.
years.xp: The label was wary of its growing reputation as a home for bands that no longer existed. The album waited thirteen years. One track slipped out on a 1989 benefit compilation.

years.h: Canty takes the drum stool in Fugazi
years.p: He replaces Colin Sears in [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]]'s new band.

years.h: All Through a Life · Dischord No. 22
years.p: The January 1986 session finally comes out as a 7-inch, a year after the band is gone. The same year's CD and cassette of the LP fold these songs in, plus one more, Other Way Around.

years.h: [[Happy Go Licky|4c18be5e-2e53-41a4-a4a1-d9080ff88f8c]]: the original four, off the map
years.p: All four Rites of Spring members, back together under a new name and playing something much stranger: tape loops, sound effects, songs that were largely or entirely improvised. They never set foot in a studio.

years.h: Picciotto starts singing with Fugazi
years.p: He's on stage with them by their second show and joins for good once Happy Go Licky winds down.

years.h: Happy Go Licky's last night
years.p: New Year's Day at the 9:30 Club. After that, the Rites of Spring story continues only in Fugazi.

eras.title: Back out of the drawer
eras.text: With Fugazi drawing crowds around the world, a lot of new listeners went looking for where Picciotto and Canty came from. Dischord gathered the Rites of Spring recordings onto one disc and slowly let the side projects out too.

years.h: End on End: everything on one disc
years.p: Seventeen tracks: the LP, the single and Other Way Around, under the title most fans know it by now. Dischord still files it as No. 16. A remaster follows in 2001.

years.h: Happy Go Licky, finally on Dischord
years.p: Will Play collects live recordings from the band that never made a studio record.

years.h: One Last Wish's 1986, thirteen years late
years.p: The album recorded in November 1986 finally comes out on Dischord, named for the only year the band existed.

eras.title: The word they never asked for
eras.text: By the 2000s, emo was a word on magazine covers, and Rites of Spring kept getting named as where it started. The band wanted none of it. Meanwhile the vault gave up the very first tape.

years.h: Fellows as Miighty Flashlight
years.p: After years of session work around the Drag City label, Fellows releases a self-titled album as Miighty Flashlight.

years.big: A genre with their name on it. They never signed up.
q: I've never recognized 'emo' as a genre of music.
years.h: Picciotto rejects the label
years.p: Asked about being called the first emo band, Picciotto flatly refuses the premise.
years.xp:
In a 2003 interview he said every band he'd played in was simply a punk rock band. His counterexample: nobody would say the Bad Brains weren't emotional.

[[Jenny Toomey|246fc8dd-a667-4a5b-868a-a5897bcd6c59]] put it plainly: Rites of Spring existed well before the term did, and they hated it.

years.h: Six Song Demo · Dischord No. 176
years.p: The April 1984 tape, 28 years later, on 10-inch vinyl and download. End on End, All There Is and By Design, the first songs they ever wrote, in their first recorded form.
